headline: Iran-Hormuz rejection and oil spike snap last week's rally mood
body: US equity futures turned lower to start the week after President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, undercutting the optimism that had carried the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to their best weekly gains since early August. Brent crude jumped roughly 4% toward $108 a barrel and WTI rose a similar amount near $96, reviving the inflation-and-shipping-cost anxiety that had only briefly eased on hopes of a negotiated de-escalation. Dow, S&P, and Nasdaq-100 futures each slipped in early trading, and the cautious tone carried overseas, with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi falling alongside broader Asian equities. The move reads as a reflexive repricing of geopolitical risk rather than a shift in the underlying growth story, but it's a reminder that last week's advance was leaning on a de-escalation narrative that has not been confirmed.

Beneath the daily headline, the macro backdrop stays uneasy: consumer sentiment is hovering near historic lows around 48, households are penciling in inflation expectations above 4.5%, and both the 10-year Treasury yield and 30-year mortgage rates sit above 5% and 7% respectively, keeping financing costs elevated even as headline indices flirt with record territory. Renewed AI-safety commentary from industry leaders, which triggered a sharp chip-stock selloff earlier this month, continues to hang over sentiment toward the megacap names that have driven most of the market's gains. Retail-forum trackers didn't surface a clear, dominant single-stock narrative for today specifically, so this read leans more on the oil/geopolitical headline and the softening macro data than on any fresh wave of social-media positioning.
